question: Should OpenClaw permit `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` on non-loopback or private-ingress Gateway binds, and if so what explicit guardrail or acknowledgement is required?
rationale: The request would move Gateway operator-surface protection from OpenClaw auth to external network controls, crossing an intentional auth boundary that current source, tests, docs, and audit checks preserve.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Default
options.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and direct private deployments to the supported delegated-auth path.

options.title: Sponsor Private-Ingress Opt-In
options.body: Allow reachable no-auth only behind a deliberately named high-risk policy with startup warnings, security audit findings, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Reject this trust model in core and close the request after documenting the supported token/password and trusted-proxy alternatives.

recommendation.title: Keep Fail-Closed Default
recommendation.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and direct private deployments to the supported delegated-auth path.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history on the relevant Gateway auth hardening and no-auth exposure boundary.
